title: A City-paid business at the address of a barred contractor
question: After the City suspends or bars a contractor, does another business registered at the same address collect City money?
finding: 1 business(es) registered at the exact address of an organization on the City’s suspended, debarred or agreed-not-to-contract lists began receiving City payments around or after the action; the largest, OBS Engineering Inc, shared the suite from 2018-07-02 to 2020-02-01 and has been paid $3.5 million since Azul Works, Inc’s 2020 action (2 long-standing co-tenants that were already City payees are left out). Separately, 8 City-paid businesses took over the address and part of the name of a closed business; those read as ordinary reorganizations (a sole owner incorporating, a sale, a merger) and are not listed.
how: Organizations named on the City’s Suspended and Debarred Contractors page and in the Controller’s semi-annual reports are looked up in the Treasurer’s business registration file. Any other registration at the identical address and suite (12 or fewer registrations ever) that was open there at the same time for at least 90 days, and whose name matches a City payee first paid no earlier than the year before the action, is listed with City payments before and after the fiscal year of the action.
limits: Sharing a suite or a yard is not shared ownership: small contractors sublet desks and yards from larger ones, and the Treasurer’s file does not name officers. The listed contractor may have moved out before the City acted. A suspended firm may finish contracts it already holds. The test to run next is the State contractor licence and Secretary of State officer records for the two firms, which are not in this file.
